Last week we witnessed one of the most striking ruptures in the alliance between the tech and political worlds: the public blowout between Trump and Musk. After pouring hundreds of millions into Trump’s campaign and serving as a special adviser on the “Department of Government Efficiency" Musk is now on the outs with Trump and his future within the MAGA movement is uncertain.

At 3:00am this morning, Musk began groveling for forgiveness. He posted on X, “I regret some of my posts about President realDonaldTrump last week. They went too far.”

Brace Belden is the co-host of the podcast TrueAnon and has been covering Elon and the right wing internet universe for years. He joined me on this week’s podcast to break down Musk's rise in the MAGA world, the big blowup, what this fracturing means for the right going forward, and what's next for Elon. Watch here!

Right wing creators are dominating L.A. protest coverage

There are very few reporters in Los Angeles compared to cities like New York and Washington D.C., and even fewer local journalists. Layoffs at major local outlets like The Los Angeles Times, along with the full dismantling of smaller local outlets have left the city with an extremely limited number of reporters.

While the few remaining local journalists on the ground are getting shot and going to the hospital to have “less lethal” rounds removed from their bodies, right wing content creators are swarming in, creating videos that are amassing millions of views and reshaping the narrative about the protests on platforms like X, Instagram, and YouTube.

Eli Tan at the New York Times reports:

As protests in Los Angeles against the Trump administration stretched into their fifth day on Tuesday, social media creators have at times outnumbered the traditional press corps at rallies and have played an outsize role in sharing media about what has happened on the ground.

Outfitted with their own makeshift press helmets and vests, many creators — many of whom lean conservative — have livestreamed entire days of coverage and posted to social platforms like X and streaming sites like Twitch and YouTube. During some of the week’s most violent moments, Trump officials like Stephen Miller and billionaires like Elon Musk chose to amplify what the creators published, causing the posts to go viral and feeding the narrative that the violence has been out of control.

Among the creators at the protests was Cam Higby, 25, a journalist and political commentator for the conservative digital outlet Today Is America. He flew to Los Angeles from his home in Washington State on Friday after seeing videos of the demonstrations on X.

On Monday night, he livestreamed from the front lines of the protests alongside another online creator and friend, Aldo Buttazoni, 25. Mr. Higby and Mr. Buttazoni previously worked for the conservative media outlet Prager U and brand themselves as “America First 🇺🇸.” Much of their content comes in the form of rebuttals to Democratic officials like the mayor of Los Angeles, Karen Bass, or Mr. Newsom.

Mr. Higby’s posts, which have amassed millions of views in recent days, blur the line between reporting and advocacy. He sometimes posts video updates about police movements, and other times repeats Mr. Trump’s statements about how “LA NEEDS THE NATIONAL GUARD,” in attempts to stoke outrage.

I’ve reported for years on this disparity and witnessed it myself even back in 2017, when I covered over 60 protests that year for The Hill. Digital media was still booming back then, but social media was already where people were getting their news, and creator content was already outperforming that of traditional media. The far right, which recognized this early, was pumping millions into the creator economy while Democrats mocked influencers.

Major news events like the L.A. protests show just how dangerous this disparity in coverage is. There is zero left wing creator ecosystem to meaningfully counter these right wing efforts. While right wing creators can get their flights and hotels paid for by wealthy donors to cover protests and major news events on the ground, left-leaning content creators and independent journalists are struggling to make ends meet.

Assuming they can even muster up the resources to go cover an event, left wing creators and independent journalists have to pay for 100% of their travel, accommodations, and legal fees if they get detained. There is zero support network for them, and the Democrats, including all the Democrat donors, don’t seem interested in building one. Instead, they’re focused on pumping millions into middleman organizations and centrist creators who repeat DNC talking points and frequently bash journalism.

Funding independent journalism that actually challenges power is more important than ever, and we desperately need people with resources who care about protecting Democracy to step up.
